description:
Create a mechanical documentation check, register it as the `docs-mechanical` gate, and cover it with self-tests.

## Background

No mechanical check exists for documentation links, citations or projection freshness. The check is a stdlib-only Python script under `contrib/gates/`. It reads its documentation footprint from `.jit/config.toml` and delegates JIT-specific checks to the `jit` CLI (`jit item show` for addressable references, projection rendering for freshness).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The script reports broken Markdown links, broken heading anchors, missing repository-local file citations, unresolvable `@/` item references, and stale invariant and rule/gate projections, each as a distinct failure class with file and line.
- [hard] REQ-02: The footprint is read from configuration and covers the root and crate READMEs, `docs/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, Markdown under `dev/active/`, and repository-relative links inside Rust doc comments; `dev/archive/` is excluded.
- [hard] REQ-03: Fixture-based self-tests cover a clean tree, every failure class, a missing or failing `jit` binary, and projection drift; the fixtures contain no hand-maintained inventory of real product facts.
- [hard] REQ-04: `docs-mechanical` is registered as an auto gate, and the self-tests run as part of the gate or of the Rust CI gate.
- [hard] REQ-05: Findings in the current tree are fixed or, where their only location is material the documentation migration archives, listed in a linked record; the gate passes on the resulting tree.
- [hard] REQ-06: `jit invariant check`, invariant projection, the documentation review, `docs-mechanical` and `jit validate` all pass together on the resulting tree.

## Decisions

- DEC-01: The user decided on 2026-10-02 that the missing-citation class applies to the permanent documentation surface only (root and crate READMEs, `docs/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`); links, anchors and `@/` item references are checked across the whole footprint, including `dev/active/` Markdown. Code-span paths in development records are historical text, not citations. The three deliberate quotations of unresolvable addresses in development records are listed in the temporary baseline record.
title: Add the docs-mechanical gate with self-tests
